findings.title: A later good identity is placed after the deed
findings.claim: The focus presents the brothers' projected goodness as a temporal separation: the removal is placed on one side of the after-phrase while a righteous group identity is reserved for what comes later.
findings.mechanism: The focus afterness carrier joins the projected righteous-state carrier and the two removal commands; later supplied scenes of accountability, demonstrated good conduct, confession, and intercession return through those focus words and make the proposed interval a semantic relation rather than a bare sequence marker.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the brothers treating time as a moral partition, with a future label imagined to follow and settle the present act.
findings.containment: The finding describes the brothers' projected logic, not a general rule that later repair is impossible. The later records keep actual accountability and repair visible, and no single later outcome is ranked as the only interpretation.

epistemic.reason: The cross-run finding and focus branch records are trusted, while the reader-walk corroboration and wider contextual connections are legacy-unbound or target-surface-only; the relation is therefore retained with explicit qualification.

branch_activations.boundary: The after-phrase remains temporal afterness; it does not by itself prove repentance or specify the antecedent of its pronoun.

findings.title: Paternal regard is imagined as an occupiable place
findings.claim: The removal alternatives are made to serve a zero-sum picture in which Joseph occupies the father's face and regard, so clearing him away appears to make that valued place available to the brothers.
findings.mechanism: The focus killing and emptying carriers meet the face construction, the supplied 12:10-12 disappearance sequence, later remembrance contacts, and face-status parallels; the contact turns removal from a bare alternative into an attempted clearing and reassignment of paternal attention.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive the brothers' motive as a spatial model of affection and standing: one person's removal is imagined to release both attention and the position attached to it.
findings.containment: The ordinary killing, casting, emptying, and face readings remain intact. The spatial and status model describes the brothers' construal and does not establish that affection is actually transferable or that the listed face parallels share the same full setting.

epistemic.reason: The activation records are legacy-unbound, while the focus carriers are supplied and the wider connection targets provide exact Arabic surface evidence without target morphology; the relation is retained as qualified contextual resonance.

findings.title: Repair arrives as a relation
findings.claim: The focus's promised later goodness is given a distinct wider counter-reading by the supplied later turn to confession, forgiveness, and intercession: repair is enacted between persons rather than achieved by simply waiting for the deed to become past.
findings.mechanism: The afterness and righteous-state carriers return through the exact 12:92, 12:97, and 12:98 connections, where released reproach, a request for forgiveness, and a father's promised prayer supply relational acts that the focus's future label leaves unstated.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can distinguish a calendar change from moral repair and can see why the focus's final promise remains an unfulfilled projection at this point in the story.
findings.containment: This does not replace the focus's ordinary future projection or declare one complete theory of repentance. It preserves the separate possibilities of confession, forgiveness, and intercession as the supplied later evidence presents them.

epistemic.reason: The retrospective support is legacy-unbound, while the later connection rows provide exact Arabic surface evidence and authored relation notes without target morphology; the finding remains qualified.

findings.title: The cleared place keeps the absent person
findings.claim: The focus's imagined emptying is later exposed as incomplete: the father's remembering and search keep Joseph present, and the returning garment reaches the very face whose vacancy the brothers had planned.
findings.mechanism: The focus emptying and face carriers meet the supplied 12:85, 12:87, and 12:93 records, whose exact connection notes trace persistent remembrance, continued search, and the garment placed on the father's face; the wider sequence reverses the expected clean vacancy.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see absence itself becoming a carrier of presence: moving Joseph away does not remove him from the father's face or from the story's route of recognition.
findings.containment: The reversal is a wider contextual resonance, not a denial that the brothers intend removal. The target rows supply exact Arabic surface and connection notes but not full target morphology, so the sequence is not expanded into unprovided lexical claims.

epistemic.reason: The focus-side activation is supported by a legacy-unbound wide reader walk and supplied same-surah connection records whose target morphology is absent; the reversal is therefore qualified.
